name: Cerise
lede: Cerise is the French word for cherry, borrowed into English as the name of a strong pinkish red.

sections.title: A cherry that is not a cherry
sections.body:
*Cerise* is simply French for cherry [1]. Paterson's dictionary notes that the color word is not necessarily the color of the fruit, and that it usually means a bluish red or a purplish red [1]. The ordinary English word for the fruit's own color is `cherry`, and Paterson sends readers from [[cherry]] to cerise [2].

The first example in the Oxford English Dictionary, as recorded in our name data, is a Times report of 1858 [3]. No book we read says what the word first described, so we do not claim a dye or fashion link [3].

sections.title: A word for lips and wine
sections.body:
Pastoureau observes that modern lipstick shades are named after fruits, with cerise, redcurrant and raspberry among the French examples [4]. Paterson gives Chianti as a dark cerise [2].

St Clair's bibliography points to an essay by Kory Stamper on how Webster's Third defined colors, with cerise as its test case [5]. We have read only the citation, so we do not report her findings.

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The swatch here is a vivid pink-red, close to [[crimson]] and [[magenta]] in feel [3]. Nothing in the books fixes cerise at one exact color, so treat it as a region of the pink-red range, not a point [1]. It is brighter and pinker than [[red]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive has this color covering at least 1% of its canvas, as photographed [6]. That describes the archive, not painting as a whole [6]. In printed English the noun peaks in the 1920s and the adjective in the 1930s, in Google Books counts [6]. The color is also listed in Maerz and Paul (1930) and the ISCC-NBS system (1955) [3].

origin.first_recorded: 1858, The Times, the OED's first example (per our name data)

disambiguation.gloss: Cherry is the fruit's color; cerise leans bluer

questions.q: What does cerise mean in French?
True or false: cerise is exactly the color of a cherry.

openers: Cerise is French for cherry, yet dictionaries say the color usually runs bluer than the fruit.
